output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the failure of the east-side chiller (CH-2), which left floors 6-8 at 26-29 C from 4 to 19 August. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1 and overall from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores on those floors recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. Floors 1-5 barely moved. Cleanliness and check-in scores, inspection pass rates, kiosk queue times and complaint counts about them are flat, so the housekeeping contractor and the kiosks are not the cause. Neither should be removed on this evidence. The survey method was unchanged. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value-for-money down slightly on floors 1-5, but that drop is close to the usual August dip, so I can't separate the two. Don't reverse the rate on this evidence. I'm fairly confident (about 85-90%) in the cooling diagnosis. Next steps: restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Don't exclude the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. Keep watching value scores through September. I collected no extra evidence because the initial evidence already settled the main questions.
